title: Classify seven residual Schur-pair states and full-guard counts (no new κ)
body:
PR #4678 leaves the simultaneous-conjugacy state after Schur deletion open. This six-file package answers that handoff for the binary commuting projector pair with joint-sector dimensions **(1,1,1,2)**. It finds seven ordered residual-pair orbits, retains their complete-header multiplicities, and counts the two remaining scalar guards. No new kappa.

The sample space is all **9,999,360** complete GL5(F2) headers for a fixed pair of rank-three projectors. Full guards require both requests' leading minors of orders 1, 2 and 3 to be nonzero.

- **93,564** headers pass every guard: exact fraction **2599/277760**.
- The credited sharp one-block event has **60,480** headers. It reaches one orbit of **5,040** residual pairs with multiplicity **12** each; **3,240** headers continue through all guards, a conditional **3/56**.
- Commutator rank loses continuation information: two rank-zero states have full-guard fractions **5/28** and **61/3360**. Two other distinct states even share all displayed individual/product/sum/commutator ranks; their common-kernel dimensions distinguish them.

`README.md` proves the completion-fibre/orbit multiplicity reduction and guard equivalence. `RESULT.json` records all 172 admitted split pairs and their state assignments. The independently written standard-library checker imports no predecessor code. The contribution is the state distribution and continuation count; PR4678's one-block count is corroborated and credited.

### Validation

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/schur-residual-orbits
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/schur-residual-orbits --check-source-history
```

Normal and optimized registered replays pass. Coverage includes all **496** split pairs, full GL4 orbits, **141,120** literal complete-header checks using direct leading-minor determinants, an independent determinant census of **65,536** binary 4-by-4 matrices, and seven rejection controls. The direct header checks cover one full completion fibre per orbit; the written equivariance argument extends the counts to all split pairs. This is not a raw enumeration of all GL5 headers.

Committed bytes/source history, official export integrity, and a fresh Git-free optimized export replay are checked before publication. The export replay has an empty PATH, reads read-only files, and leaves every file hash unchanged. Detailed environment and overlap coverage are in TASK.json; hosted CI is reported separately after creation.

### Scope and coordination

Started from canonical main `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7. The [scoped claim in Discussion #4653](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4653#discussioncomment-19126925) takes PR4678's fresh handoff. `formal-interface-lemma` is explicitly changed to an algebraic side result. Final upstream/overlap freshness is recorded in TASK.json. The selected result remains **0.00302015**.

This proves a finite classification with an exact counting reduction, not a general state recursion, physical supplier, human/proof-kernel acceptance or multiplication theorem. F2 is outside the retained odd-q normalizer executable domain. Production header covers, selection/emission, reads, restoration, stock, dispatch and complete consumer costs remain unknown. Lean, Docker and the selected scientific cold replay were not run. The open next question is an invariant-based transition law reproducing this table without enumerating GL4; no follow-up claim is held.

Credit **ssafwann** (#4678/#4671, OpenAI Codex assistance), **Nick Petalas** (#4597/#4278 and earlier header lineage), **Ryanson Jonathan** (binary sharpness and full-guard census, Claude Code assistance), **lee-phys** (binary dimension work), and **Cinna Davis** and the credited normalizer lineage. Exact citation/source pins are included. Prepared for **Mihir Srivastava** with substantial **OpenAI Codex** assistance, by one agent. Apache-2.0.
